scope: aggregate-only K-Means output governance, approved features, complete-case population accounting, small-cell privacy, arbitrary cluster-ID semantics, numerical stability, stale-model clearing, source immutability, internal assignment diagnostics, and cross-product integrity
confirmed_findings_fixed: Publishable clustering results could contain employee-level cluster assignments; publishable results are now aggregate-only.
Cluster IDs could be rendered through persona-like names that implied stable workforce types; output now states that unsupervised group IDs are arbitrary and are not risk levels or personas.
Small clusters and within-cluster department cells lacked an explicit privacy publication floor; cells below five are now suppressed from aggregate output.
Clustering population exclusions were not structurally disclosed; source population, complete-case analysis population, exclusions and coverage are now explicit.
Extreme-but-finite feature magnitudes could destabilize standard scaling or aggregate means; stable pre-scaling and finite-output checks now fail closed.
Cluster-count input validation now rejects booleans, non-integers and incompatible counts rather than relying on downstream library behavior.
Failed retraining clears stale model, label and result state before returning failure.
Feature selection is restricted to an explicit approved measurement set so numeric identifiers cannot silently enter the clustering geometry.

Internal engineering diagnostics preserve employee-to-cluster assignments only behind a neutral Cluster N naming boundary; governed product API routes remain aggregate-only and block membership access.
interpretation_boundary: Clusters are exploratory aggregate geometry over approved measured features. Cluster numbers are arbitrary labels, are not employee risk categories, causal groups or validated workforce personas, and are not an employment-action recommendation.
remaining_scientific_limits: K-Means geometry remains sensitive to feature selection, scaling choices and the assumed Euclidean structure of the measurements.
Synthetic cluster recovery and silhouette quality do not establish organizational construct validity or stable workforce personas.
Longitudinal stability, resampling stability and organization-specific use-case validation are required before enabling cluster outputs as a product decision surface.
Individual cluster membership remains an internal diagnostic only and must not become an employee ranking or consequential-decision signal.
